description.narrative:
Tekoindustrin är Bangladeshs största exportindustri och ger arbete åt drygt fyra miljoner människor varav ca 80 % är kvinnor. Industrin har kritiserats för låga löner och brister i arbetsvillkor och -miljö, säkerhet och fackliga rättigheter. Arbetsmarknadslagstiftningen är otillfredsställande, även om Bangladesh har antagit de flesta ILO-konventioner. Någon fungerande förliknings- eller tvistlösningsmekanism finns inte. Efter Rana Plaza katastrofen finns dock ett starkt momentum inom sektorn att förbättra arbetstagarnas säkerhet och rättigheter med tryck från utländska köpare och regeringar. ILO har sedan Rana Plaza drivit ett omfattande program för att förbättra reformprocessen gällande arbetsrätt och relaterad lagstiftning och praxis.
Det övergripande syftet av projektet är att stärka arbetsmarknadsrelationerna och den sociala dialogen mellan arbetsgivare och arbetstagare inom tekoindustrin. Förväntningen är att detta ska bidra till ökad produktivitet, stärkta rättigheter för arbetstagare och förbättrade arbetsvillkor och arbetsmiljö. Projektet ska genomföras på tre nivåer; i) den nationella och där fokusera på förändringar inom regelverk samt stärkta institutioner och policy utveckling, ii) sektoriella och då främst fokusera på att bygga organisationskapacitet och forum för dialog mellan arbetsmarknadensparter och på iii) fabriksnivå för att stärka den sociala dialogen mellan arbetsgivare och arbetstagare. Projektet är utvecklat utifrån en ansats att den sociala dialogen mellan arbetsmarknadens parter är ett viktigt medel för att stärka arbetstagarnas rättigheter på arbetsplatser, medverkan i demokratiska beslutsprocesser för arbetstagare och för att öka företagens produktivitet. Icke-fungerande fackföreningar, bristfällig tillämpning av arbetsrättsliga regleringar och rådande sociala normer bidrar till att många fattiga män och kvinnor står utan representation på arbetsplatsen. Risken för att behandlas illa är stor och kvinnor är särskilt utsatta. Könsrelaterat våld och diskriminering på arbetsplatsen är vanligt förekommande. En annan viktig fråga för projektet är att öka den nuvarande låga andelen kvinnor i ledande positioner i fackföreningar, arbetsplatskommittéer och arbetsgivarorganisationer.
Projektet genomförs av ILO i nära samarbete med den bangladeshiska regeringen, utvalda arbetsgivarorganisationer och fackförbund i nära samarbete med IF Metall och H&M. Det senare har stark närvaro i Bangladesh och kommer att bidra med värdefull kunskap, erfarenhet och nätverk inom tekoindustrin. Projektet löper över fem år med start i november 2015 med en inledningsfas på sex månader. Sverige och Danmark är de huvudsakliga givarna till projektet varav Sveriges andel av budgeten är 70 %, motsvarande 45 miljoner kronor. Projektet har en innovativ ansats främst genom samarbetet med H&M och förhoppningsvis andra mulitnationella företag i branschen. Projektet förväntas ge intressanta lärdomar bortom det enskilda projektet samt representerar en tillämpning på landnivå av Sveriges Global Deal initiativ om att stärka arbetsmarknadsrelationer globalt och kommer att bidra till SDG 8.

The Ready-Made Garments (RMG) sector is Bangladesh's biggest export industry and provides work for more than four million people of whom about 80% are women. The industry has been criticized for low wages and poor working conditions, safety and trade union rights. Labour legislation is unsatisfactory, although Bangladesh has acceded to most of the ILO conventions. A functioning conciliation or arbitration mechanism does not exist. After the Rana Plaza disaster, there is a strong momentum in the sector to improve workers safety and rights of pressure from foreign buyers and governments.
The overall Project objective is to strengthen industrial relations and social dialogue between employers and workers in the RMG sector. The expectation is that this will contribute to increasing productivity, strengthening the rights of workers and improving working conditions. The Project will be implemented at three levels: i) national, with a focus on improving in the regulatory framework and institutional and policy development, ii) sectorial, with focus on building organisational capacity and forums for dialogue between the social partners and iii) factory, with focus on strengthen the social dialogue between employers and employees. The Project is based on a hypothesis that social dialogue between the social partners is an important means for advancing human rights in the workplace, increasing workers participation in democratic decision processes and increasing business productivity. Non-functioning trade unions, poor application of the labour law regulations and prevailing social norms contributes to that many poor men and women are without representation in the workplace. Young people and women are often particularly vulnerable and gender-based violence and discrimination in the workplace is common practice. Another important issue for the Project is the low proportion of women in leading positions in trade unions, workers participation committees and employers' associations.
The Project is implemented by the ILO in close collaboration with the Bangladeshi government, employers' associations and trade union federations in close collaboration with IF Metall and H&M. The Project will run for five years starting in November 2015 with an inception phase of four months. Sweden and Denmark are the main donors of the Project, whereof Sweden's share of the budget is 70%, equivalent to SEK 45 million. The Project is innovative and can provide interesting lessons beyond this Project and it represents an application at country level of Sweden's Global Deal initiative to strengthen labour market relations globally and will contribute to SDG 8.

The project is funded by the Governments of Sweden and Denmark and runs from October 2015 to December 2022. One year after the signing of the agreement, with ILO as implementing partner, the project was linked to the Global Deal initiative - an initiative launched by Swedish Prime Minister Stefan Löfven on 21 September 2016. The Global Deal is a global multi-stakeholder partnership with the objective of jointly addressing the challenges in the global labour market and enabling all people to benefit from globalization, in line with SDG 17 (partnerships for the goals) in Agenda 2030. It is also a concrete input to several of the other goals, not least SDG 8 on Decent Work and Inclusive Growth and SDG 10 on Inequalities. As Bangladesh joined Global Deal, the country wanted several concrete actions to highlight within their commitment. The Social Dialogue and Harmonious Industrial Relations in the Bangladesh Ready-made Garment Industry Project, SDIR, was one of the interventions that the Government of Bangladesh reported as a committment. SDIR - Social Dialogue and Harmonious Industrial Relations in the Bangladesh Ready-made Garment Industry
The SDIR project's overall objective is to contribute to the development of an effective industrial relations framework and social dialogue in the Ready-made garment sector in Bangladesh. The project has three overarching expected outcomes:
Outcome 1: Sustainable improvement in social dialogue, workplace cooperation and grievance handling; Outcome 2: Sustainable and effective mechanisms for conciliation and arbitration are established; Outcome 3: Enhanced capacities of employers' and workers' organizations to dialogue and prevent and resolve disputes, including those of gender concern.
To reach the objectives the project team implements various activities, including trainings in grievance handling and international labour law, implementation of Standard Operating Procedures for registration of unions, establishment of a Tripartite Consultative Council, Participation committees and a Workers' Resource Centre.
In March 2020, the Covid-19 pandemic reached Bangladesh on a full scale. For that reason, the project was amended to address the emerging needs in the wake of the Covid-19 crisis. The Embassy decided to grant ILO an additional 7 MSEK for Covid-19 related activities and at the same time extend the activity period until 30 June 2021. In the RMG sector, the ILOs response includes a joint response with BGMEA BKMEA, DOL and the WRC through the implementation of a training and monitoring initiative to support the RMG industry and its work. The following areas are covered by the Covid response part of the project: 1) Factory outreach of COVID-19 related training packages to 410 factories, 2) COVID-19 Awareness OSH Managing labour relations Development of a COVID-19 Communication and Advocacy strategy, 3) Community level outreach to workers community, 4) Support the formation of a trade unions rights watch team.
The project period under the program was set to 30 June 2021 but due to delays due to the pandemic and other, the Embassy during summer 2021, conducted a no cost extension where the project period was extended until end of 2022 to increase the probability for the project to reach its intended objectives, complete delayed activities, as well as adding on some additonal activities that could further support the overarching objective of the project while responding to prevailing challenges on the labour market and in the RMG-sector. The project is also supporting the national action plan to alleviate the identified deficits in the area of labour rights by supporting the strenghtening of the local union work to the benefit of workers in the workplace.

The key project milestones achieved up to March 2023 are:
Outcome-1:
482 factories (171 unionized and 311 non-unionized) enrolled to SDIR project, 147 national master trainers (40% female) developed on diverse training modules promoting social dialogue and industrial relations. 30 Department of Labour (DoL) officials trained as master trainers of Workplace Cooperation training module. DoL master trainers trained 595 bipartite representatives (41% female) of Participation Committees of 38 RMG factories. 100% of trained factories concluded gender sensitive workplace cooperation plans. 1669 bipartite representatives (50% female) of 415 RMG factories trained on Grievance Handling. However, measure for effective grievance handling procedures in place in the trained factories, is yet to be established. 574 TU and management representatives (38% female) of 152 unionized RMG factories trained on Collective Bargaining and Negotiation Skills. However, no CBAs concluded to date with the support of the project. 292 factory-level TU leaders (46% female) of 137 unionized RMG factories trained on Trade Union Administration.
Outcome-2:
The project supported the establishment of the RMG Tripartite Consultative Council (RMG TCC) in March 2017. SoP on TU registration developed and incorporated in BLA (amended in 2018). SoP on investigation of anti-union discrimination and unfair labour practices developed and incorporated in BLA (amended in 2018). 30 DoL Officials trained on investigation of unfair labour practices. 30 national conciliators established, as part of a pool at DoL. On-line publicly accessible database on registered Trade Union (regularly updated by DoL) expected to be launched in this year. Support to DoL, with technical assistance, in the development and implementation of the GoB GB Roadmap and EU National Action Plan. A 3-day residential workshop was facilitated in March 2022, having both MoLE and DoL officials, to frame a draft SoP for Conciliation to be incorporated in the Labour Law. As a result of the workshop a draft was developed that is pending for approval from MoLE. DoL has facilitated technical sessions for WRC TB members 3 days in a row on 3 specific subject matters (7-9 August 2022) on 2 SoPs and Publicly Accessible Database). SDIR-ILO has organized these sessions. A day-long training was facilitated for the newly appointed Conciliators of the DoL (31 August 2022).
Outcome-3:
Workers Resource Center (WRC) established in 2017 and fully operational. 67 TU representatives (60% female) trained by the project as WRC master trainers on the following subject matters. Grievance Handling: 20 (including 13 females) Collective Bargaining and Negotiation Skills: 18 (including 11 females) Best HR Practices: 10 (including 05 female); and TU Administration: 19 (including 11 female) In collaboration with the Centre for Advanced Legal Studies (CALS) of Dhaka University and ITCILO, the project trained 27 trade union representatives as Paralegals to facilitate addressing dispute related issues raised by RMG workers. Until May 2021, the trained paralegals facilitated 721 grievance complaints and dispute related issues, out of which, 478 disputes settled (including group cases) benefitting more than 11,000 workers (52% female). 50 officials (40% female) nominated by BEF, BGMEA and BKMEA trained as master trainers on the following subject matters. Grievance Handling: 08 (including 04 female) Collective Bargaining and Negotiation Skills: 10 (including 04 female); Best HR Practices: 09 (including 03 female); and Supervisory Skills: 23 (including 11 female). 1344 Production Supervisors (20% female) of 404 RMG factories trained on effective Supervisory Skills. 1428 HR officials and worker representatives (39% female) of 411 RMG factories trained on Best HR Practices and IR.
SDIR projects initiatives under ILO-Dhaka COVID-19 response to the RMG sector:
The Project provided technical support in drafting of National Labour Relations Guidelines amid COVID-19 pandemic, which is now waiting for the approval of Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE). The project, under RMG clustered approach, initiated COVID-19 Training Package and developed 164 tripartite master trainers (29% female) for capacity building of RMG workers and employers on COVID-19 awareness, OSH, and labour relations issues to guide the sector for a safer return to work. Until May 2021, the trained master trainers outreached. 418 RMG factories with COVID-19 awareness training, covering total 1672 worker management representatives (47% female); 403 RMG factories with Return-to-Work OSH training, covering total 1612 worker-management representatives (47% female); and 394 factories with Managing Labour Relations training, covering total 1576 bipartite representatives (44% female). In collaboration with BRAC, the project developed COVID-19 awareness behaviour change communication materials; and implementing an advocacy campaign targeting 5000 HHs (covering 20000 Population) of selected RMG workers community at Gazipur and Chattogram. The Project provided support in drafting the Terms of Reference (ToR) of Trade Union Rights Watch Team (TURWT), formed by WRC to provide coordinated support to the workers in challenges relating to industrial relations: unfair labour practices, anti-union discrimination, unlawful dismissals, during the ongoing and post COVID-19.
Final evaluation report 2022
In 2022, the final of evaluation of the project was conducted from 28 August 2022 to 31 December 2022 and the final report was submitted on 28 December 2022. The independent international and national evaluator were hired to assess and evaluate the Projects implementation for its entire duration, i.e., from 2017 to 2022. Below are some aggregated results of the program as concluded by the evaluation:
The evaluator has found that there is a mutual leveraging and complementarity coherence among SDIR and other ILO projects in the RMG sector and it has been able to adapt to contextual changes during implementation, as when the COVID -19 virus started spreading in March 2020. Complementarity also exists between the different streams/themes of work under the three outcomes, and synergy e.g., in terms of cooperation of the involved stakeholders. The Project contributed to the establishing of the National Tripartite Consultative Council and the RMG Tripartite Consultative Council in 2017, to institutionalize social dialogue in the sector.
The Project was instrumental in supporting the Government in setting up of Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) on Trade Union Registration and Investigation of Anti-Union Discrimination, and Unfair Labour Practices. GoB has included these SOPs in the 2018 amended Bangladesh Labour Act (BLA). The Workers Resource Centre (WRC) is a brainchild of the Project, set up in cooperation with NCCWE and IBC in 2017.
Another successful result is that Paralegals (trained in 2019 and 2021) linked to the WRC have been able to help resolve many disputes at enterprise/factory level and thus prevented workers´ complaints to go into the national machinery and end up at the Labour Court where the backlog reportedly is more than 19,000 pending cases.
The project has supported to set up the National TCC and a RMG TCC to have real and long-lasting impact, these need to be fully active - which requires commitment from the tripartite partners to hold meetings and discussions as intended. The two SOPs that were integrated into the BLA, are examples of tangible impact, which led to a rise in membership of basic unions from 2012 to 2019. The Publicly Accessible Database is likely to have an impact in the sense that it contributes to transparency on labour market information.
In 2022 a final evaluation the Covid-related work under the program implemented by BRAC was finalized which showed important outcomes due to communication and advocacy work among women workers of how to prevent and protect against Covid. Exampl of a result revealed that knowledge and practices on COVID-19 prevention was improved by > 20% on multiple aspects except wearing of mask by pregnant women.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
